introduction.text: Welcome to your first hiragana lesson! The A-row consists of the five basic vowel sounds in Japanese.
introduction.text_ja: 最初のひらがなレッスンへようこそ！あ行は日本語の5つの基本母音です。

characters.mnemonic: Looks like an A with a hat!

content.summary: You've learned the five basic hiragana vowels: あ, い, う, え, お. Practice writing them and recognizing them!

exercises.question: Which hiragana character makes the 'a' sound?
exercises.question_ja: 「あ」の音を表す文字はどれですか？
exercises.explanation: あ (a) is the first hiragana character and makes the 'ah' sound like in 'father'.

exercises.question: What does 'いい' (ii) mean?
exercises.question_ja: 「いい」はどういう意味ですか？
exercises.explanation: いい (ii) means 'good' in Japanese. It's a common word you'll use often!

exercises.question: Match the hiragana to its sound
exercises.explanation: Practice these sounds: う (u), え (e), お (o)

title: Hiragana K Row (Ka, Ki, Ku, Ke, Ko)

introduction.text: Now that you know the vowels, let's add the K consonant to create the KA row!
introduction.text_ja: 母音を学んだので、次はK音を加えてか行を学びましょう！

content.summary: You've learned か, き, く, け, こ - the K row of hiragana!

exercises.question: Which character represents 'ki'?
exercises.explanation: き is the hiragana character for 'ki'.

introduction.text: Learn essential Japanese greetings to start conversations!
introduction.text_ja: 日本語で会話を始めるための基本的な挨拶を学びましょう！

items.usage: Polite morning greeting, use at work

items.japanese: ありがとうございます
items.usage: Polite thanks, use in formal situations
Formal goodbye, when you won't see them soon

content.summary: Master these greetings and you can start basic conversations in Japanese!

exercises.question: What is the polite way to say 'good morning'?
exercises.explanation: おはようございます (ohayou gozaimasu) is the polite form of good morning, used in formal settings.

exercises.question: When would you use 'こんばんは'?
exercises.explanation: こんばんは (konbanwa) means 'good evening' and is used in the evening hours.

exercises.question: How do you say 'thank you' politely?
exercises.correct_answer: ありがとうございます
exercises.explanation: ありがとうございます (arigatou gozaimasu) is the polite form of thank you.

title: Introduction to Particles: は and を

introduction.text: Particles are essential in Japanese - they show the relationship between words in a sentence.
introduction.text_ja: 助詞は日本語で非常に重要です。文中の言葉の関係を示します。

sections.title: The Topic Particle は (wa)
sections.content: は marks the topic of the sentence. Note: it's written は but pronounced 'wa'!

examples.reading: わたしはがくせいです。
examples.breakdown: 私 (I) + は (topic marker) + 学生 (student) + です (am)
これ (this) + は (topic marker) + 本 (book) + です (is)

sections.title: The Object Particle を (wo)
sections.content: を marks the direct object of an action. Pronounced 'wo' or 'o'.

examples.breakdown: 本 (book) + を (object marker) + 読みます (read)
水 (water) + を (object marker) + 飲みます (drink)

content.summary: は marks the topic, を marks the object. These are your first steps to building Japanese sentences!

exercises.question: 私___学生です。 (I am a student)
exercises.explanation: は marks the topic 'I', so 私は学生です is correct.

exercises.question: 水___飲みます。 (I drink water)
exercises.explanation: を marks the object 'water', so 水を飲みます is correct.

exercises.question: Which particle marks the topic of a sentence?
exercises.explanation: は (wa) is the topic particle in Japanese.

introduction.text: Learn to count from 1 to 10 in Japanese!
introduction.text_ja: 1から10まで日本語で数えましょう！

content.summary: Practice counting 1-10 until it becomes natural!

exercises.question: What is the number 'san' (さん)?
exercises.explanation: さん (san) means three in Japanese.

exercises.question: How do you write 'five' in kanji?
exercises.explanation: 五 is the kanji for five, pronounced 'go'.
